## Offload policy (main conversation only)

Delegate before pulling large sources, logs or command output into this context, because every token here is the most expensive one. Subagents cannot dispatch subagents: they do this work themselves.

| Situation | Delegate to |
|---|---|
| Searching or reading more than 3 files, or an unfamiliar codebase | `explorer` (built-in role) |
| Running tests, lint, typecheck, a build or another read-only command that you expect to take over a minute or to print more than a screen of output (spawn it, keep working, and collect its result before your final answer) | `check-runner` |
| Reading any file over ~200 lines (logs, docs, PDFs, large diffs, source) to answer from it, map it, or pull out a part you cannot locate with grep | `summarizer` |
| Any web search or web page | `researcher`, one per question, in parallel |
| Writing the code of a plan task (more than ~20 changed lines), even when it looks easy | `implementer`: write its brief, then review its diff instead of writing the code yourself |
| Mechanical lint/type/test fixes after a change | `fixer` |
| Verifying a changed web UI in a browser | `ui-verifier` |
| Before executing any plan, spec or design | `pre-mortem` |
| Before your final answer, whenever you or a worker (e.g. `implementer`) changed the project since its last review: code, docs, files, a deletion. The review is part of done, because the author is anchored on its own reasoning and a fresh context sees what it no longer does. Spawn it together with the checks and collect its result before your final answer, triage every finding yourself and verify the medium/high ones in one call that prints every cited range, except for plan-loop fix rounds (see Routing). A change a review already covered is not reviewed again. After fixing, re-run it once only when the fix reaches beyond the findings (it touches a file or behavior no finding named) (round 2 is the last); otherwise confirm the fix by reading it and the checks | `skeptical-reviewer` |

Keep inline: decisions, edits under ~20 lines, integrating results, reading a range you located with grep, and a short check with its output cut (`| tail`, `-q`), because a dispatch costs more than its few lines. A task whose design is still open is not delegated: settle it here, or ask the owner, then brief it.

Every call re-reads this whole context, so count calls before tokens:

- Join commands that do not need each other's output in one shell call, and send independent tool calls in one message. A lookup of up to ~3 steps stays here as one call.
- Delegate an episode you expect to take eight or more calls of your own (twelve when the worker writes code), or to print more than ~8k tokens you will not need word for word, when a short answer can replace it. A dispatch costs this context about as much as five to eight of your calls (brief, report, notices and what you re-read afterwards), so smaller work is cheaper batched here. A row above that names its own threshold (a long file to `summarizer`, a long command to `check-runner`, plan code to `implementer`) applies instead of this rule for its case, and `skeptical-reviewer` has no size threshold: it reviews every change; this rule covers the rest.
- Give a worker one outcome. Split a brief with several goals or more than about five focus points, because a worker that runs out of turns returns nothing.
- When you have nothing to do until a worker returns, wait with `wait_agent`, which wakes on any worker's message, instead of writing messages in between, because each one re-reads this context.

Spawn every worker with `fork_turns` set to `"none"`, because the default copies this whole conversation into the worker and makes its first request nearly five times larger. The worker then sees none of this conversation, so its brief carries what only this conversation knows:

1. **Goal** and acceptance criteria it can check itself: one outcome per brief.
2. **Scope**: the paths it owns, and what it must not touch.
3. **Decisions already taken, each with its reason**, so it neither reopens nor contradicts them.
4. **Checks**: the commands that prove the result.

Name a file the worker can open (a committed plan task, a spec, a commit range) instead of restating it, and write out only what exists nowhere but here. Every worker already has its stop rule and its report format: state one only to change it. For a built-in explorer, request the answer with its decisive source and any uncertainty that changes the next action. A brief to `explorer` (built-in role) still states a length, because that agent's report format is not ours on every tool.

State the what, the limits and the check, not each step: the worker reads the code and works out the how. Independent briefs run in parallel in one message, with disjoint paths.

Before you reply: if the project changed since `skeptical-reviewer` last ran, other than a fix confined to the findings it reported, dispatch it now.
